2011_016_020111regmtg.paragraph: Agenda and supporting packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held February 1, 2011 at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. Business included appointing a replacement for Board member Carol Pochodylo, who resigned January 3, 2011, for a term ending December 31, 2011; closing Athens and Troy High Schools to open enrollment for 2011/2012 with an exception for up to 30 incoming ninth graders; continuing Headlee/Adair litigation; and a carpet bid award. The centerpiece is the 2010-11 budget amendment resolution, which appropriates $135,897,825 in the General Fund and amends the Special Revenue, Debt Service, Capital Projects and Internal Service funds.

**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, February 1, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

**Recognition and Board vacancy**
Wendy Underwood was honored for service as Board president from July 2009 to January 2011, a period noted for 42 National Merit Scholar Semi-finalists, more than 600 students and staff recognized in tournaments and competitions, an added freshman class at the International Academy East Campus, formation of a district-wide Diversity and Inclusion Council, and Michigan Association of School Boards Standard of Excellence and Visionary Leadership awards. Following Carol Pochodylo's January 3, 2011 resignation, the Board took nominations and a roll-call vote (Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming) to appoint a member for the term expiring December 31, 2011.

**Consent agenda minutes**
January 18, 2011 organizational meeting (called to order 7:00 p.m., adjourned 7:12 p.m.): Philippart elected president, Edmunds vice president, Fleming secretary, each 5-0 with Hauff absent; Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, appointed Treasurer for January through December 2011; fund depositories, deputy secretary designation, Judy Brill designated to post notices, and the 2011 meeting calendar adopted (resolutions 11-001 through 11-009). January 18, 2011 regular meeting (7:13 p.m. to 9:25 p.m.): 72 senior fall scholar athletes and 10 all-state athletes recognized; Schools of Choice resolutions under Sections 105 and 105C; an intergovernmental services agreement with Avondale School District for July 1, 2010 through June 30, 2011; Edline web hosting at $29,436.00; PRI local and long distance service to Paetec - Tampa at $59,118.55. January 21, 2011 Board retreat, 6:01 p.m. to 10:48 p.m., Administration Building.

**Open enrollment**
Athens High School and Troy High School recommended closed to open enrollment for 2011/2012, except for not more than 30 incoming ninth graders residing in the Troy High attendance area who wish to attend Athens; 25 spots had been made available for 2010/2011. Applications accepted February 2-18, 2011; siblings of Athens students in grades 9-11 also permitted.

**2010-11 budget amendment**

| Fund | Amended appropriation |
|---|---|
| General Fund | $135,897,825 |
| Special Revenue Funds | $5,530,101 |
| Debt Service Funds | $18,596,717 |
| Capital Projects Fund | $7,216,120 |
| Internal Service Fund | $120,000 |

General Fund revenue, approved vs. amended vs. change: Local $44,378,692 / $43,855,326 / ($523,366); State $70,443,859 / $71,324,198 / $880,339; Federal $10,371,927 / $11,574,529 / $1,202,602; Incoming Transfers/Other $9,114,130 / $9,609,420 / $495,290; total $134,308,608 / $136,363,473 / $2,054,865. Total expenditures move from $135,793,505 to $135,897,825, a change of $104,320. Excess revenues/(expenditures) goes from ($1,484,897) to $465,648, and ending fund balance June 30 from $16,635,541 to $19,326,709.

**Other business**
Headlee/Adair litigation: Troy is one of 467 districts suing the State of Michigan over underfunding of special education and other mandated services under Article IX, Section 29; $55,455.10 spent to date; an additional $5,000 authorized for Secrest, Wardle, Lynch, Hampton, Truex & Morley. Carpet replacement in the Morse Elementary media center (Bid 9698) recommended to Conventional Carpet at $28,300.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. A 2011-2012 budget-reduction communication plan set dates of February 8 (School Finance 101), February 23-25, March 1, March 7-10, March 15 and April 19. First reading of revisions to Board Policy G-1003, Nepotism. Closed session on negotiations under the Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c).

**Meeting**
Board agenda for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of February 1, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district address 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., except in July and August. Agenda: recognition of Wendy Underwood; appointment of a Board member; consent agenda minutes; Enrollment Projections and Schools Closed to Open Enrollment; the 2010-2011 Budget Amendment, Headlee/Adair litigation and a carpeting bid award; budget-reduction communication; first reading of Board Policy G-1003, Nepotism; and closed session on negotiations.

**Recognition - Wendy Underwood**
Wendy Underwood served as president of the Troy Board of Education from July of 2009 to January 2011. The citation notes 42 National Merit Scholar Semi-finalists in the past year, more than 600 students and staff members recognized in tournaments and competitions, another freshman class added at the East Campus of the International Academy, a district-wide Diversity and Inclusion Council, the continuing North Central Accreditation process, and Board honors including a Standard of Excellence Award from the Michigan Association of School Boards, a Visionary Leadership Award and recognition for commitment to the Fine Arts for the third year in a row. Recommendation: distribute token of recognition.

**Board vacancy**
Due to the resignation of Mrs. Carol Pochodylo on January 3, 2011, the Board must appoint someone to serve through the end of her term, ending December 31, 2011. Nominations are limited to one candidate per member, followed by resolutions closing nominations and appointing, with a roll call listing Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Underwood, Edmunds and Fleming.

**Organizational meeting minutes, January 18, 2011**
President Underwood called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building; Edmunds, Fleming, Miletti and Philippart were present, Mr. Hauff absent, along with Superintendent Fowler, administrators Birmingham, Bryan, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter, Stromayer and Witt, and approximately 65 audience members. Resolution 11-001 made Ms. Underwood acting chairperson (Ayes 5, Nays 0, Absent Hauff) and Judy Brill temporary secretary. Ms. Philippart was elected president (11-002), Mrs. Edmunds vice president (11-003) and Mrs. Fleming secretary (11-004), each until December 31, 2011 by roll call 5-0. Resolution 11-005 appointed Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, as Treasurer for January through December 2011; 11-006 adopted the Fund Depositories and Investments resolution for the same period; 11-007 continued the Superintendent of Schools as Deputy Secretary for the 2011 calendar year; 11-008 designated Judy Brill, Secretary to the Superintendent, to post meeting notices; 11-009 adopted the 2011 meeting schedule. Adjourned 7:12 p.m.; submitted by Judy Brill, Acting Secretary, and Paula Fleming, Secretary.

**Regular meeting minutes, January 18, 2011**
President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:13 p.m.; Mr. Hauff was absent. The Board recognized 72 senior scholar athletes from fall sports who maintained a 3.5 cumulative grade point average, among them Madhav Achar, Caitlyn Berard, Ashley Bezrutch, Jessalyn Camp, Adam Cowherd, Alexander Hatzis, Saabir Kaskar, Giuliano Mancini, Bridget Richards, Kaushik Varadarajan and Perry Zong. All-state fall athletes were Sean Cunningham (Boys Soccer), Alec Bezerra (Boys Soccer), Jacob Duzey (Football), Kelly Feng (Girls Golf), Brett Forman (Boys Tennis), Matthew Kuntzman (Boys Tennis), Kento Mizusaki (Boys Tennis), Monique Nguyen (Volleyball), Matthew Smolinski (Boys Soccer) and Jennifer Yang (Girls Golf). For National School Board Recognition month the Board itself received cards created by district art students and a short video.
Resolution 11-010 approved the consent agenda: minutes of the December 6, 2010 Board meeting and December 14, 2010 workshop, and the Treasurer's Report for November and December 2010 (Ayes 5, Nays 0, Absent Hauff). Resolutions 11-011 and 11-012, under Sections 105 and 105C of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, accepted applications for a limited Schools of Choice program for 2011/2012 for nonresident kindergarten and first grade students within Oakland County and from contiguous intermediate school districts. Mrs. Jennifer Gottlieb, science coordinator, reported on the NASA DIME Competition in March 2011 at NASA's Glenn Research Center in Cleveland, Ohio, using the 2.2 second drop tower; the Troy High School team was one of four nationally selected and travels to Cleveland March 21-25, 2011 with teacher John Morrison.
Resolution 11-013 authorized an agreement with Avondale School District for management, consulting and supervisory services relative to Avondale's administrative services for one year starting July 1, 2010 and ending June 30, 2011, with an option to renew. Resolution 11-014 awarded the web hosting bid to Edline for $29,436.00 from the 2010/11 General Fund; Mr. Bryan noted a four-year option at the same cost and a 38% discount for renewing existing service in advance. Resolution 11-015 awarded PRI Local and Long Distance Service to Paetec - Tampa for $59,118.55 against the 2011/12, 2012/13 and 2013/14 General Funds. Student representative Andrew Michail reported Troy High's Snowcoming Dance on February 12th, the "Go Blitz" Global Outreach fundraiser on February 25th for a hospital in Africa, State Conferences March 26-27th, Powder Puff and Battle of the Bands. Members thanked Mrs. Pochodylo, relocating to Pennsylvania, and noted 16 applicants for the trustee seat and a Martin Luther King, Jr. Day Celebration at Athens organized by Kerry Birmingham. Resolution 11-016 approved Ms. Philippart's attendance at the National School Boards Association Annual Federal Relations Network Conference in Washington, D.C., February 6-8, 2011; 11-017 scheduled a Special Board Meeting for Tuesday, January 25, 2011 at 7:00 p.m.; 11-018 moved the Board into closed session on negotiations under the Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), 5-0. Closed session began at 8:08 p.m., the meeting reconvened at 9:24 p.m. and adjourned at 9:25 p.m.

**Board retreat minutes, January 21, 2011**
President Philippart called the workshop to order at 6:01 p.m. at the Administration Building with Edmunds, Fleming, Miletti and Underwood present and Hauff absent; also attending were Superintendent Fowler and administrators Birmingham, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter, Witt and Papasian, plus two audience members. Topics: public communication; the 2010/2011 First Appropriation Act, including Adair litigation; finance, covering budget projections and the 2011/2012 budget; the budget communication plan; nepotism policy revisions; and Board self-evaluation. Adjourned 10:48 p.m.

**Schools closed to open enrollment, 2011/2012**
Both high schools have been closed to open enrollment for the past three years; for 2010/2011, 25 spots were made available for students scheduled to attend Troy High School but wishing to attend Athens. The 2011/2012 recommendation again closes Athens High School and Troy High School except for not more than 30 openings for incoming ninth graders living in the Troy High attendance area who wish to attend Athens, with applications accepted February 2-18, 2011. Students with siblings at Athens currently in grades 9-11 may also open enroll there.

**Headlee/Adair litigation**
Troy is one of 467 school districts suing the State of Michigan over continued underfunding of special education and other mandated services under the Headlee Amendment, seeking a declaratory judgment under Article IX, Section 29 of the Michigan Constitution; an amended complaint has been filed with the Court of Appeals. Prior cost limitations: May 12, 1998, $5,000; March 2, 1999, $10,000; June 20, 2000, $10,000; September 19, 2000, $10,000; August 20, 2002, $10,000 (an additional $10,000 beyond the previous $35,000); February 5, 2008, $10,000. The district has spent $55,455.10 to date. The resolution authorizes Secrest, Wardle, Lynch, Hampton, Truex & Morley to continue representing the district, with its pro rata share not to exceed an additional $5,000.

**Carpet replacement bid award**
Bid 9698 for carpet replacement in the Media Center at Morse Elementary was opened January 24, 2011; nine potential bidders were solicited and three responded, none "No Bid." Conventional Carpet bid removal/disposal $1,950.00 and installation $26,350.00 for a total of $28,300.00; Shock Bros. Floorcovering bid 1,500.00 removal, 5,400.00 installation and 27,100.00 material, total $34,000.00; Shamrock Floorcovering bid 1,794.00 removal and 38,052.00 installation, total $39,846.00. No response came from Fair Way Tile & Carpet, Floor Craft Floor Covering, Macias Floors, Quality Floor Covering, Tri-County Floor Covering and Wilkins Floor Covering. A January 26, 2011 memorandum from Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget (1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052, fax 248-823-4077) to Mark S. Rajter reports that Ken Miller, Director of Operations, recommended award to Conventional Carpet as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund.

**Budget reduction communication plan, 2011-2012**
Goals: inform parents, staff and community about the budget process, proposed reduction areas and changing economic conditions; solicit and acknowledge input; and provide transparency. Vehicles include www.troy.k12.mi.us with a "Budget 2011-2012" homepage icon, past budget reductions, focus group results and community input, plus Finance 101 sessions, community meetings in each quadrant, traditional and social media, email lists and publications. Timeline: February 8, School Finance 101; February 23-25, communication to administrators and impacted employees; March 1, budget presentation at the TSD Board meeting; March 7, 8, 9 and 10, community meetings at each middle school; March 15, report back to Board; April 19, authorization to implement reductions.

**First reading, Board Policy G-1003, Nepotism**
The Policy Committee updated Board Policy G-1003, General Section G-1000, Number 1 (Covers All Employees), Policy Regarding Newly Hired Employees - Nepotism; the Board's attorney reviewed the changes against state law, the Open Meetings Act and the Revised School Code. As of December 6, 2005, no person may be newly hired or promoted into any position if a close relative is employed as an administrator by the district or contracted as one through a third party, excepting temporary employment of high school and undergraduate college students during school recess. "Close relative" covers father, mother, husband, wife, son, daughter, sister, brother and the corresponding in-law relationships, by blood or adoption; "administrator" means a position designated as administrative in Section C-1101 of the Board Policy Manual. The policy applies to permanent (full or part-time), substitute, temporary and student employees, and "promoted" reaches any current employee or third-party-contracted administrator who could be offered a C-1101 position or one with increased supervisory functions. The Superintendent may grant exceptions for interim appointments. Adopted October 20, 1981; revised December 6, 2005, June 19, 2007 and February 2011.

**Closed session**
